In pre-modern Japan, the leaves were boiled as a vegetable first, and served with a salad of grated yamato (white sweet potato) that has been coated in salt. After eating raw yamato was never eaten by oneself unless served as a condiment with other foods, so in order to make sure the sesame seed coating remained dry you put it on the green leaf first and eat the leaf only after you are satisfied that the sesame seed coating is dry. 3) Fava "Fava" or "black bean", is one classic ingredient in Greek food. Its ingredients include green pea root, kale, beans and garlic among others. The plant part which is used to make this dish is called "black bean" as it doesn't change the appearance of its stalks once cooked and it retains its black color even as the stalks break and become small pieces in the soup. The other ingredient which is added before cooking is kale (which goes under different names in other countries such as "broccoli" and "cauliflower"). This ingredient is named for its dark color which is different from the white kale that could be found in the stores. Some ingredients used in Greek cuisine such as fava beans, potatoes, and tomatoes also contain genes that make them easier to digest for people with digestive problems. The Greek doctors say this helps people to digest this food more quickly and reduce their risk of getting intestinal problems, especially in the winter time, this disease is called "Epsom-Ramsay-Hunt syndrome". Also as with other countries' dishes, there is usually some meat added to the fava dish, such as eggplant, anchovies or some type of fish.
4) Gyro Gyro ("Greek food") is a dish with Greek ingredients and a Greek name with Greek letters as an ingredient. In the western world the most famous Greek dish with these ingredients and named according to the Greek letters is the tzatziki sauce. To preserve the food longer it has been cooled down to below freezing and then covered with a layer of olive oil. This keeps the food from rotting. In Greek dishes there is usually only half the amount of oil compared to what is used in the western world foods. The Greeks believe this helps the food last longer, and also that the flavor of the food will be more concentrated as the oil has less the ability to remove flavors by mixing it with other ingredients.
